feed.title: Testing & QA — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: An annotated directory of links on software, AI, security and science. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Applitools Demo
entry.summary: A demo designed for visual testing, comparable against a second version. Unlike functional testing it targets catching changes in how the screen looks.

entry.title: Awesome k6
entry.summary: A resource list for k6, the developer-centric load and performance testing tool. Unlike general performance lists it focuses on one tool and its scripting ecosystem.

entry.title: Awesome Playwright
entry.summary: A list of tools, plugins and examples for the Playwright ecosystem. Unlike the official docs it brings together community tooling and real project examples.

entry.title: Awesome QA Roadmap
entry.summary: A roadmap gathering how to start and grow a career in software testing. Unlike tool lists it draws an ordered learning path.

entry.title: Awesome Selenium
entry.summary: A collection of the Selenium browser-automation framework and its surrounding tools. Unlike scattered search it gathers language bindings, grid and plugins in one place.

entry.title: Awesome Testing
entry.summary: A list gathering every branch of software testing — unit, end-to-end, performance, contract — with resources. You can also find the rest of this field’s practice sites here.

entry.title: Coffee Cart
entry.summary: A simple app for practising basic interactions through ordering coffee. Unlike large demos it is small enough to grasp in five minutes yet full enough for cart/logic testing.

entry.title: DemoQA
entry.summary: A broad automation practice set with forms, widgets, interactions and a bookstore app. Unlike single-page sites it has enough variety to exercise a whole framework end to end.

entry.title: GoREST
entry.summary: A test API with OAuth2 authentication and write support, over REST and GraphQL. Unlike read-only fake APIs it truly lets you exercise create/update flows.

entry.title: Insomnia
entry.summary: A clean API client for REST, GraphQL and gRPC requests. Unlike Postman it is lighter and open source, and can be versioned with git.

entry.title: JSONPlaceholder
entry.summary: A zero-setup test API that returns realistic fake JSON on request. Unlike running your own mock it is instantly available — the standard for prototypes and tutorials.

entry.title: ParaBank
entry.summary: A sample banking test site that ships with SOAP/REST services. Unlike simple demos it is suited to testing web services, WSDL and workflows.

entry.title: PokéAPI
entry.summary: A large, deeply nested REST API serving Pokémon data — popular for tests and tutorials. Unlike simple fake APIs its rich, related data model lets you exercise realistic queries.

entry.title: Postman
entry.summary: A desktop/cloud tool to build, store as collections and test API requests. Unlike curl it saves requests, holds environment variables and runs automated test sequences.

entry.title: Practice Software Testing
entry.summary: A realistic tool-shop demo with both a UI and a REST API, designed for end-to-end testing. Unlike older demos it runs on a modern stack (React + API + Swagger).

entry.title: randomuser.me
entry.summary: An API generating any number of fake users (name, address, photo). Unlike fixed fixtures it returns varied, realistic data on each call — for form and list tests.

entry.title: Reqres
entry.summary: A hosted REST API that answers AJAX requests, with pagination and delay simulation. Unlike JSONPlaceholder it can also emulate response delays and error states.

entry.title: Restful-Booker
entry.summary: A test API emulating room booking, with authentication and good docs. Unlike fake APIs it includes writes and auth — a full CRUD flow can be exercised.

entry.title: Rick and Morty API
entry.summary: A free API serving character, episode and location data over both REST and GraphQL. Unlike single-protocol APIs it exposes the same data two ways, letting you test both.

entry.title: Sauce Demo
entry.summary: A sample shopping site with ready logins for learning automation; some users deliberately misbehave. Unlike random demos its scenarios are stable and repeatable.

entry.title: SelectorsHub · XPath Practice
entry.summary: A page deliberately hardened for practising complex XPath and CSS selectors. Unlike general demos it contains selector hells like nested iframes and shadow DOM.

entry.title: SSL Labs Server Test
entry.summary: A test that scans a site’s TLS configuration and grades it A–F. Unlike the browser padlock it gives detail at the level of certificate chain, protocols and cipher suites.

entry.title: Swagger Petstore
entry.summary: The canonical sample API with a Swagger UI front end — the standard place to learn OpenAPI. Unlike other fake APIs its interface is generated straight from the spec.

entry.title: The Internet (Herokuapp)
entry.summary: A classic practice site collecting the common scenarios that challenge automation (iframes, file upload, hovering menus) one by one. Unlike demo shops each page teaches a single difficulty.

entry.title: UI Test Automation Playground
entry.summary: A site exposing the traps that trip up automation on the modern web (delayed load, hidden elements, dynamic ids). Unlike general demos it targets exactly “why is my test flaky”.

entry.title: WebPageTest
entry.summary: A test measuring a page’s load performance from real devices and locations. Unlike Lighthouse it gives a waterfall, filmstrip and multi-location comparison.
